I fixed the float rounding in the sales report and committed it as `b952352`.

The report is `SalesReport` in `src/orders-api/sales_report.py`. It summed float prices directly, which produces the binary approximation errors. Now each price is converted through `str()` into a `Decimal`, and totals are rounded to cents. So `0.1 + 0.2` reports as `0.30`.

One visible change: totals now always show two decimal places, so `4` reports as `4.00` rather than `4`. That matches the `0.30` format you asked for, but if you want whole numbers to stay bare, that's a small change to make. I updated the existing test expectations to match and added a test for the float case. All 9 tests pass.

I left two things uncommitted: your edit to `README.md` (the "Note to self" line) and the `notes/` directory. The `quarterly_export.py` module also sums prices with plain `sum()`, so it will show the same artifacts. I didn't touch it because it isn't the report you described, but I can apply the same fix there if you want.
